AUD 236.desc: Observations in UC San Diego Otology clinic. Learn about procedures for taking histories and performing clinical examinations, patient treatment, and patient education from otologists.
AUD 236.pre: second-year AuD student or consent of instructor.
AUD 236.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 257.desc: Differential diagnosis and treatment of auditory and vestibular disorders, audiological components of neuro-otology, as well as interactions between the audiologist and neuro-otologist in a clinical setting.
AUD 257.pre: second-year AuD student or consent of instructor.
AUD 257.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 260.desc: This course describes advanced assessment including tinnitus assessment, tuning fork tests, Eustachian tube dysfunction tests, sound sensitivity assessment, and automated audiograms. Assessment methods, clinical research, and pathology will be discussed. Students will gain hands-on experience through laboratory assignments.
AUD 260.pre: second-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

AUD 263.t: Physiological and Behavioral Tests of Vestibular Function
AUD 263.desc: Clinical evaluation of vestibular function, using techniques such as caloric and rotational electronystagmography and posturography. The interpretation of clinical findings and implications for rehabilitative strategies will be covered. The course will include observation of testing in otology clinic settings.
AUD 263.pre: second-year AuD student or consent of instructor.
AUD 263.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 271.desc: Detailed anatomy of the temporal bone, cranial nerves and basic neurophysiology for audiologists. Radiographic and magnetic resonance imaging of the temporal bone will be discussed.
AUD 271.pre: second- or third-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

AUD 272.t: Central Auditory Processing Assessment and Management
AUD 272.desc: Central auditory processing assessment and management for pediatrics and adults. Focus on behavioral tests assessing dichotic listening, temporal processes, pattern recognition, performance with competing and degraded signals.

AUD 274.t: Advanced Technical Aspects of Hearing Amplification
AUD 274.desc: Advanced technical aspects of assessing and fitting amplification devices for the hearing impaired. Intensive hands-on training to develop skills necessary for audiology clinical placement.
AUD 274.pre: course restricted to AuD students or consent of instructor.
AUD 274.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 275.desc: Methods and procedures required for monitoring of evoked auditory responses in the operating room. The indications for the use of intraoperative monitoring and difficulties unique to this setting. The course will include the opportunity to observe auditory potential monitoring in the operating room.
AUD 275.pre: second- or third-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

AUD 276.t: Cochlear Implants and Other Implantable Sensory Aids
AUD 276.desc: Theory and practice of cochlear implantation with focus on audiological management of patients after implantation. Current concepts regarding the activation of primary auditory neurons by electrical stimulation and indications for cochlear implantation and surgical procedures are described.
AUD 276.pre: second- or third-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

AUD 278.desc: Current and developing topics in audiology introduced in group projects, presentations, and mock clinical scenarios. Improving grasp of audiology underpinnings, business practices, critiquing treatments, and emerging technologies.
AUD 278.pre: second- or third-year AuD student or consent of instructor.

AUD 284.desc: Applications of clinical procedures to patient assessment. Includes clinical observation, interaction with otologists, and supervised patient care involving diagnostics and hearing-aid evaluations in the UC San Diego audiology clinics. This course may be taken more than once.
AUD 284.pre: open to second- or third-year doctoral students or consent of instructor. One quarter unit represents three to four hours per week. Must also be concurrently enrolled in AUD 291.
AUD 284.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 291.desc: Presentations and discussion of clinical cases and issues related to clinical practice. Students’ clinical experiences are discussed relative to medical and audiological assessment and management. This course may be taken more than once.
AUD 291.pre: second- or third-year AuD student or consent of instructor. Must be taken more than once.
AUD 291.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 296.desc: Participation in specific faculty research activities. Become familiar with research methods and objectives of a faculty’s research project. Participate in data collection and analysis at the discretion of the faculty investigator.
AUD 296.pre: second- or third-year AuD student and consent of instructor.
AUD 296.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 298.desc: Independent research on topics relevant to audiology, consisting of literature review, data collection. Faculty supervision and mentoring on practical elements of research design and methodology. The course will consist of laboratory experience, focused on practical elements of research and design and methodology.
AUD 298.pre: consent of AuD program adviser and consent of faculty mentor.
AUD 298.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)

AUD 299.desc: Individual investigation and preparation of the doctoral project for the AuD degree will be performed under the supervision of an experienced research mentor.
AUD 299.pre: advancement to candidacy in the AuD program.
AUD 299.res: Limited to academic level: Graduate; Limited to major: Audiology (Jnt. Doc SDSU)
